P3-ID-FIX-SENTENCE: After every experiment had run, a verification check found that cargo ids were not unique: 9–18 of about 2,970 items a year reused an earlier id, in every regime (change 10 of the pre-registration). Ids enter the simulator's decisions only through a planning memo within one dispatch call. The fix was tested by rerunning 48 full years (E40, E43: every regime or mode, seeds 1–3), of which 48 gave outcomes identical item by item, compared by content without ids; reused ids fell from 670 to 0. No experiment was rerun and no reported number changes; trace and scene files written before the fix still carry the duplicate ids.
P3-H10-VERDICT-SENTENCE: H10, exploratory, holds on every count: the safety check at 41.8 % of one core of the reference processor at the worst class (the crew rover), the on-robot part at 0.4 MB of 256 MB, and the radio traffic at 7.68 kbit/s for 20 robots against the 16 kbit/s target, and the market's messages at 0.005 MB a day against the 1 MB target, with the scaling factor at 54.8 (range 36.5–64.0); the bidding, which H10 also names, has no registered capacity (Section 5.1 reports the scaled round against the one-second decision).
P3-E48-ROUND-SENTENCE: Scaled by the same factor, an auction round on the crew rover takes 0.11 s at the median and 1.12 s at the 99th percentile, above the one-second decision that the link model of Section 5.3 assumes.
P3-E48-REFERENCE-SENTENCE: The reference flight processor is the Frontgrade Gaisler GR740 (rad-hard quad-core LEON4FT, 250 MHz), at 492.5 CoreMark per core (source: Cobham Gaisler, GR740 benchmark results, ESA DSP Day 2016: 1.97 CoreMark/MHz/core x 250 MHz) with 256 MB of memory (Assumed: SDRAM of a typical GR740 single-board computer); the laptop is an Intel Core i5-10500H (6 cores, 2.5 GHz base, 4.5 GHz turbo) at 27,000 CoreMark per core, itself assumed (Assumed: 4.5 GHz turbo (Intel spec) x 6.0 CoreMark/MHz (typical for this core generation; no published CoreMark for this chip found), range 4-7 CoreMark/MHz); the factor is their ratio, 54.8, with the range 36.5–64.0 from the laptop's CoreMark range, and the CPU share uses the 99th-percentile call time at every call, so it is an upper bound (Assumed).
P3-E48-MTBF-SENTENCE: The failover sweep runs the base computer at an MTBF of 500 h, 2,000 h, 8,000 h, a repair time of 24 h and a re-election delay of 0.5 h, on five seeds of C_LEADER, message loss 0.1, 30 % load, 1x, one year, flagged Assumed (B-72 defaults; sweep); the re-election delay is an input, not a measurement.
P3-E48-HORIZONS-SENTENCE: The instrumented runs last 365 days at 1 times today's fleet, 90 days at 4 times today's fleet, 60 days at 8 times today's fleet; the ledger's yearly growth at four and eight times is extrapolated from jobs per hour.
P3-E48-TRAFFIC-NOTE: The status message at the assumed 1 Hz is 99.99 % of the messages and 99.99 % of the bytes at 1 times, 99.88 % of the messages and 99.92 % of the bytes at 4 times, 99.62 % of the messages and 99.72 % of the bytes at 8 times; the traffic counts reservation requests, grants and releases from road traversals, bids, awards and claims from auction rounds, and landing announcements, and omits rebroadcasts, team-lift proposals, answers and commits, and ledger entries.
P3-E48-RESULTS-CPU: Measured on Intel Core i5-10500H (6 cores, 2.5 GHz base, 4.5 GHz turbo) and scaled to the Frontgrade Gaisler GR740 (rad-hard quad-core LEON4FT, 250 MHz) by a factor of 54.8 (range 36.5–64.0, Assumed): across the four robot classes a safety check took 577 µs–583 µs at the median and 693 µs–763 µs at the 99th percentile over 20,000 calls per class, worst on the crew rover; an auction round took 1.98 ms at the median and 20.5 ms at the 99th percentile over 84,367 rounds; the on-robot part peaked at 0.39 MB. The base computer's reservation check over the shared table, a different function from the vehicles' safety check, took 136 µs at the median and 191 µs at the 99th percentile, and its auction round 1.98 ms and 20.5 ms (Table 5).
P3-E48-RESULTS-MESSAGES: With the assumed byte layouts of Section 3.4 the message types weigh: status 48 B; reservation_request 32 B; grant 32 B; release 16 B; bid 40 B; award 32 B; claim 32 B; landing_announcement 64 B; ledger_entry 128 B. Computed from each run's event counts and the status rate, the fleet generated 3,600.3 messages and 172,812 B per robot-hour at today's fleet, 3,604.2 and 172,945 B at four times, and 3,613.9 and 173,280 B at eight times; at today's fleet that is 48.0 B/s per robot against the 100 B/s target and 7.68 kbit/s for 20 robots against 16 kbit/s. The ledger grows by 0.3 MB a year at today's fleet, 1.4 MB at four times and 2.7 MB at eight, extrapolated from each run's jobs per hour. The market's messages come to 0.005 MB a day at today's fleet.
P3-E48-RESULTS-LINK: Per class, under the models of Section 3.3, at 2.4 GHz with the data rate at the worst hop, the modelled latency of a 100-byte message (10 ms per hop plus transmit time plus the scaled safety check, against the one-second decision the model assumes) and the share of route samples in direct view of the mast: the crew rover (antenna 2.5 m, 1.00 W): 6,976 kbit/s at the worst hop, 72 ms over three hops, direct view of the mast from 23.3 % of the route samples; the cargo rover (antenna 2.5 m, 1.00 W): 6,976 kbit/s at the worst hop, 70 ms over three hops, direct view of the mast from 23.3 % of the route samples; the small rover (antenna 1.0 m, 0.25 W): 5,010 kbit/s at the worst hop, 71 ms over three hops, direct view of the mast from 19.2 % of the route samples; the hopper (antenna 1.0 m, 0.50 W): 5,988 kbit/s at the worst hop, 68 ms over three hops, direct view of the mast from 19.2 % of the route samples; the base computer (antenna 10.0 m, 5.00 W): 9,289 kbit/s at the worst hop, 20 ms over one hop, direct view of the mast from 100.0 % of the route samples.
P3-E48-RESULTS-FAILOVER: At an MTBF of 500 h the base computer was down 4.21 % of the time, the fleet had no leader 0.09 % of the time with the assumed re-election delay of 0.5 h, and the base computer's assignment table was rebuilt after repair 15.4 times a year on average over five seeds; at an MTBF of 2,000 h the base computer was down 1.10 % of the time, the fleet had no leader 0.02 % of the time with the assumed re-election delay of 0.5 h, and the base computer's assignment table was rebuilt after repair 4.0 times a year on average over five seeds; at an MTBF of 8,000 h the base computer was down 0.38 % of the time, the fleet had no leader 0.01 % of the time with the assumed re-election delay of 0.5 h, and the base computer's assignment table was rebuilt after repair 1.4 times a year on average over five seeds. After every rebuild the table held no job assigned twice.
P3-E48-DESIGN-SENTENCE: 21 runs were instrumented: six timing runs, seeds 1, 2 at 1, 4, 8 times today's fleet (C_AUCTION, message loss 0.1, roads atc (15 % single-lane), dispatch to a fixed point), and 15 failover runs, seeds 1–5 at the three MTBF levels (C_LEADER, message loss 0.1, 30 % load, 1x, one year); the auction round and the peak memory are measured once per run, not per class.
P3-E48-COMPUTE-SENTENCE: The instrumented runs of E48 took 63 s each on average and 0.1 h of processor time in all.
P3-E48-ABSTRACT-CLAUSE: Scaled by 54.8 to the reference flight processor, the safety check takes 41.8 % of one core at the worst class and the radio traffic is 7.68 kbit/s for 20 robots, within target; one auction round in a hundred takes 1.12 s, above the one-second decision.
P3-E48-INTRO-CLAUSE: Lunar ATC fits the vehicles of Section 3.2 as implemented: at the worst class the safety check takes 41.8 % of one core of the reference processor, the on-robot part 0.4 MB, and 20 robots generate 7.68 kbit/s against a 16 kbit/s-class link (Sections 5.1 to 5.3).
P3-E48-DISCUSSION-CLAUSE: the safety check, the on-robot memory and the radio traffic fit the reference processor and the link class with the stated factor, the class nearest a limit being the crew rover, while one auction round in a hundred takes 1.12 s, above the one-second decision.
P3-E48-COMPARISON-CLAUSE: The radio traffic of Lunar ATC, 48.0 B/s per robot, is 287 times smaller than the 13.8 kB/s the two-rover convoy controller of [25] used; the market's own messages come to 0.34 per robot-hour at today's fleet.
P3-E48-CONCLUSION-CLAUSE: On flight hardware the safety check and radio traffic fit the reference processor and link for 20 robots; one auction round in a hundred takes 1.12 s, above the one-second decision.
P3-E48-LIMITATION-SENTENCE: The factor used is 54.8 (range 36.5–64.0), from Intel Core i5-10500H (6 cores, 2.5 GHz base, 4.5 GHz turbo) to the Frontgrade Gaisler GR740 (rad-hard quad-core LEON4FT, 250 MHz).
P3-E48-STATUS-SENTENCE: Every measurement of Section 4.2 was made.
P3-E46-DESIGN-SENTENCE: 1,080 physical runs, 30 seeds by 2 splits by 18 run kinds (the pooled market, the oracle, the owners alone, the three pair coalitions and one owner at a time scaling its asks by each of the 4 factors); payments are computed afterwards from each run's job log, so the four rules and the 3 audit shares share one allocation per seed and cost no further runs, giving 152 cells of 30 seeds. The first-price cell is the one restored by change 7 of [59].
P3-E46-COMPUTE-SENTENCE: A simulated year of E46 took 7 s on average and the experiment 2.1 h of processor time.
P3-E46-TARIFF-SENTENCE: In E46 the posted price is 19,828.85 USD per tonne-kilometre with equal shares and 19,908.58 USD per tonne-kilometre with 50/35/15 shares, set before the main runs as the price at which the carriers' true costs are recovered over ten calibration seeds (101–110) that the main runs do not use; the audit penalty multiple is m = 3 (Assumed; the design file declares 2–5 and E46 runs one value).
P3-E46-LOSS-SENTENCE: E46 sets the message loss to 0.00 in every cell, the owners-alone and coalition runs included: a perfect radio by design, so that paired differences show incentives and not message-loss noise, which the companion paper [60] covers.

Under first price with honest asks the carriers are paid their true costs, so that budget is the tariff receipts (45.0 M USD a year with equal shares) less the true carrier cost (47.5 M USD); the tariff was set to recover that cost on the calibration seeds (Section 3.5).
P3-E46-TRANSFERS-SENTENCE: The Shapley sharing is settled by transfers between owners, Shapley payoff less the owner's cash profit under the posted price on the same seed: with equal shares owner A +112 M USD [96, 129], owner B +88 M USD [76, 100], owner C −200 M USD [−224, −176]; with 50/35/15 shares owner A +34 M USD [22, 46], owner B +44 M USD [29, 62], owner C −78 M USD [−94, −62]. P3-E46-TRANSFERS-CLAUSE: the Shapley transfers move 200 M USD a year from owner C with equal shares and 78 M USD a year from owner C with 50/35/15 shares to the other two owners

P3-E46-VS-NONE-CLAUSE: against no payments owner C is worse off under every paid rule and both splits, with the interval below zero; no other owner's interval lies below zero (A's under first price with 50/35/15 shares includes it)
P3-E46-SURPLUS-SENTENCE: With equal shares the pooling gain over alone is 804 M USD a year; under no payments owner C keeps 85 % of it (A 7 %, B 8 %, C 85 %), under the Shapley sharing owner C receives the largest share, 59 % (A 21 %, B 20 %, C 59 %), and the transfer of each owner is the difference between the two (A +112 M USD, B +88 M USD, C −200 M USD); with 50/35/15 shares the pooling gain over alone is 438 M USD a year; under no payments owner C keeps 68 % of it (A 18 %, B 13 %, C 68 %), under the Shapley sharing owner C receives the largest share, 49 % (A 26 %, B 25 %, C 49 %), and the transfer of each owner is the difference between the two (A +34 M USD, B +44 M USD, C −78 M USD).
P3-H5-POWER-CLAUSE: The cash part of that gain, with the allocation held fixed, was +2.57 M USD a year [2.43, 2.73] with equal shares and +5.40 M USD [5.01, 5.80] with 50/35/15 shares, a decomposition made after the runs (Section 4.6); the registered measure adds the deviator's own cargo delay, whose standard deviation over seeds is at least 7.6 times that cash.
P3-H5-POWER-ABSTRACT-CLAUSE: A post hoc split shows the first-price gain's cash part positive, +2.6 to +5.4 M USD, and its delay part noisy.
P3-H5-POWER-CONCLUSION-CLAUSE: A post hoc split shows that gain's cash part positive and its delay part noisy.
P3-OWN-CHECKS-SENTENCE: with every bid multiplier at 1, the market run reproduces the pooled auction exactly (A8); with one owner there are no payments between owners under any rule; the operator's budget is zero under no payments and the posted price, and under first and second price it equals the tariff receipts less the payouts, all of it between that owner and Earth (A8); the Shapley payoffs sum to the grand coalition's value on every seed (A8); asks scaled by k = 1.0 reproduce the honest payments exactly (A8); the audit at q = 0 charges nothing and at q = 1 charges m times every misreport (A8); across base-computer failures and recoveries and across mesh partitions, no cargo item is ever assigned to two jobs (the ledger itself is sized, not simulated) (A8); the E48 timers leave a run's event trace bit-identical to a run with timing off (X7) (seven checks in 9 rows; outcomes in Section 5.8).
P3-E46-RESULTS-RULES: With honest bids the four rules share one allocation, so the items delivered and the cargo delay are the same under every rule on every seed (the paired differences between rules in delay and in deliveries are exactly zero), and the market's system cost, true carrier cost plus delay cost, was above the oracle's by 12.7 % with equal shares and 35.9 % with 50/35/15 shares under every rule. Under no payments no money moved; under the posted price the budget was balanced by construction, the same tariff paid in by shippers and out to carriers. Across the three paid rules and both splits the cash settled on Earth was 6.7 M USD to 20.9 M USD a year and the balance still open at the year's end at most 0.01 M USD (Table 7).
P3-E46-RESULTS-IR: Working alone on their own cargo on the same seeds, the owners' mean profits were −106.7 M USD, −118.7 M USD and −723.4 M USD a year for A, B and C with equal shares and −141.9 M USD, −119.0 M USD and −313.0 M USD with 50/35/15 shares (alone profit is the negative of the owner's vehicle costs and its cargo's delay cost, with no receipts). Under every rule and split each owner's mean market profit (Table 7) was above its alone profit: the market left an owner below alone in 0 of the 24 owner-rule-split cases with honest bids and in 0 of the 456 owner-cell cases over every cell. Under the posted price the profit of Table 7 is the owner's Shapley value of the coalition's value, true carrier costs plus delay costs with the sign reversed, not its cash, and that value is what the Shapley clause of H5 compares with alone. In every tested coalition every owner's Shapley value was above its alone profit: the smallest difference was each of A and B's in coalition AB with equal shares, +54.2 M USD [29.7, 82.0], and the largest owner C's in coalition ABC with equal shares, +472 M USD [436, 508] (Table 8).
P3-E46-RESULTS-MANIP: With equal shares the largest gain from scaling came from owner B at k = 1.10 under both bid rules: +7.73 M USD a year [−1.46, 18.53] under first price and +6.91 M USD [−2.30, 17.71] under the per-item second price; that deviation changed the fleet's cargo delay by −5,500 h [−16,272, 3,704] and the system cost by −15.07 M USD. With 50/35/15 shares the largest gain from scaling came from owner A at k = 1.25 under both bid rules: +5.23 M USD a year [−9.72, 19.31] under first price and +2.89 M USD [−12.05, 16.97] under the per-item second price; that deviation changed the fleet's cargo delay by −72 h [−11,323, 11,596] and the system cost by +2.65 M USD. Under the posted price there is no bid to scale.
P3-E46-RESULTS-AUDITS: Under first price with equal shares an audit share of 5 % recovered 5 % of the gain, leaving +7.34 M USD and an audit share of 20 % recovered 20 % of the gain, leaving +6.18 M USD; under first price with 50/35/15 shares an audit share of 5 % recovered 15 % of the gain, leaving +4.43 M USD and an audit share of 20 % recovered 61 % of the gain, leaving +2.03 M USD; under the per-item second price with equal shares an audit share of 5 % recovered 6 % of the gain, leaving +6.53 M USD and an audit share of 20 % recovered 22 % of the gain, leaving +5.37 M USD; under the per-item second price with 50/35/15 shares an audit share of 5 % recovered 28 % of the gain, leaving +2.09 M USD and an audit share of 20 % recovered 111 % of the gain, leaving −0.31 M USD a year net of expected penalties, at a penalty multiple of 3 times the misreport.
P3-H5-VERDICT-SENTENCE: H5 clause by clause, in both splits: that first-price bids reward shading is not supported (the largest first-price gain's 95 % interval is [−1.46, 18.53] with equal shares and [−9.72, 19.31] with 50/35/15 shares, in M USD a year); that the per-item second price reduces the largest gain is supported (paired difference −0.82 M USD [−0.93, −0.70] and −2.33 M USD [−2.51, −2.13]); that the posted price with Shapley sharing leaves no owner worse off than alone in any tested coalition is supported, against the owners-alone baseline of Section 3.5 (the comparison against no payments is in Section 5.6; over every owner and coalition the smallest upper bound of Shapley value less alone profit is +82.0 M USD and +93.9 M USD, and the smallest lower bound +29.7 M USD and +36.4 M USD).
P3-H5-ABSTRACT-CLAUSE: First-price bid shading gained at most 7.7 M USD a year with an interval including zero, so that clause of H5 is not supported; the second price reduced it (supported); the Shapley clause is supported.
P3-H5-INTRO-CLAUSE: H5's first clause, that first-price bids reward shading, is not supported; its second, that the second price reduces the gain, is supported; its third, that the posted price with Shapley sharing leaves no owner worse off than alone, is supported (Section 5.7).
P3-E46-ABSTRACT-CLAUSE: Every owner beat its alone profit under every rule, but owner C fell below the no-payment market under every paid rule; the bid rules ran a deficit, the posted price broke even.
P3-E46-INTRO-CLAUSE: In the market, every rule made every owner at least as well off as alone in both splits, though owner C was worse off than under no payments under every paid rule; the operator ran a deficit under first price, a deficit under the second price and a balanced budget under the posted price (Sections 5.5 to 5.7).
P3-E46-DISCUSSION-CLAUSE: every rule left every owner's mean profit above its alone profit; the operator ran a deficit under first price (2.50 M USD a year with equal shares), a deficit under the second price (12.71 M USD, 5.1 times first price's) and a balanced budget under the posted price; the largest gain from scaling bids was +7.73 M USD a year, and audits at 20 % did not remove it under either bid rule.
P3-E46-COMPARISON-CLAUSE: The smallest owner of the 50/35/15 split gained under the posted price with Shapley sharing (+213 M USD a year [192, 236] in the grand coalition against working alone) and lost 85 M USD against the no-payment market, where Kondor's smallest operator paid the largest fleet penalty [39]; the operator's budget under the second price was a deficit.
P3-E46-IMPLICATION-CLAUSE: every rule kept every owner in; the budget was a balanced budget under the posted price and a deficit under the second price.
P3-E46-CONCLUSION-CLAUSE: Every owner beat alone under every rule, but owner C lost against no payments under every paid rule, and the largest gain from scaling bids was +7.7 M USD a year, interval including zero.
P3-E46-POSTHOC-SENTENCE: A decomposition made after the runs, not pre-registered, separates the two parts of that gain: with the allocation held fixed, the scaled asks alone paid the deviator +2.57 M USD a year [2.43, 2.73] under first price with equal shares and +5.40 M USD [5.01, 5.80] with 50/35/15 shares (+1.75 M USD and +3.05 M USD under the second price); the rest of the paired gain is the change in the deviator's own cargo delay once its asks move jobs, a term with a mean of +5.16 M USD and −0.17 M USD and a standard deviation over seeds of 29 M USD and 41 M USD, at least 7.6 times the cash, which is why the registered interval covers zero although shading pays in cash.
P3-E46-STATUS-SENTENCE: Every cell of E46 ran all its seeds.
